The + button opens the breakdown of appliances drawing power within the emitter radius.
The right-side list shows other emitters in range (link / unlink).

Real weather: sky, sun strength and temperature. More sun means chargers harvest faster.

Other KR emitters in range. Each card shows its battery, what it receives (input) and, for solar chargers, what it contributes to the generator. The button links or unlinks that unit. Multiple chargers stack their contribution with diminishing returns. Units with Generator Mode OFF are marked Storage: a unit in Generator Mode draws their internal battery when it has no sun, and their energy counts in its Reserve.
Recharge estimates: how long the internal battery takes to fill at full sun and at the current sun, and the charge time of each compatible battery.
Insert charged batteries or place a KR Solar Charger nearby.
Charging from grid power at full rate.
Move charger outdoors to use solar power.

Generator mode is off: not powering the area.
Runs on fuel: solar chargers do not contribute energy.
Electrifies metal fences, gates, doors and walls from a distance. Power 0-10 stuns, harms or burns. Paint the segments you want. Each shock wears down the segment it hits.

Each lamp has 3 alarms: zombies, animals and humans, switched on separately. Each has its own color, flash speed or fixed light, radius and sound, can stay silent or attract zombies, and can hold for a few seconds or follow movement in real time. Walls and closed doors block the sensor.

New Motion mode: the lamp turns on when something passes nearby and stays lit 8 more seconds. The light radius can now be changed from the lamp menu. All effects also run smoother and are much lighter on the game.
Every device has a new low-poly model made for Project Zomboid, with new textures and icons redone at 32x32. The old models had around 20,000 vertices; the most complex new one has 966.
The Fuel Charger, Fuel Generator and Industrial Fuel Drum can electrify too, using the fuel in their tank. They also power the Electrifier, and Kits can hold their magazines.
The Charger M, Generator and Industrial Battery can electrify too, using their own battery. Open it from the side tab of the tablet.
Safe/Lethal (right-click to change mode) and Scorched. They create a shock zone that knocks down, slows and harms.
Built from the build menu. It joins the electrifier network and wears down with each shock.
Thrown like a grenade. Lethal/Scorched (right-click to change mode). Slow to switch on and weak, but the zone lasts: a temporary barrier to seal corridors and escape.
A SolarOS fence, tougher than metal ones. It joins the electrifier network, its rods light up blue or red and it shows its damage. Zombies can still bring it down.
One magazine teaches all the new recipes.

Wiring, Structure and Power. Found as loot and opened from the inventory: they give building materials, a little Electrical XP and, sometimes, a SolarOS magazine, so you no longer depend only on libraries.

Devices now come in three looks: Sand, Tactical (black) and Commercial (civilian). Each one appears at random, and you can change it for free with Paint in the right-click menu. It is purely cosmetic. Kits and the Photovoltaic Plate keep a single look.
Defense recipes are in the Defense Schematics magazine. Full details in News, on the tablet of any device.
Electricity now defends your base. Here is what's new:
Powers metal fences, gates, doors and walls from a distance, with power from 0 to 10.
The Charger M, Generator and Industrial Battery can electrify too. It starts switched off.
Shock zones that slow, knock down and hurt.
New structures in the build menu, in the SolarOS tab.
Loot with materials and, sometimes, a SolarOS magazine.
Low-poly models in Sand, Tactical and Commercial. Change the color for free with Paint.
Alarms, Motion mode and an adjustable light radius.
Its devices can electrify too and power the Electrifier.
A reinforced SolarOS fence, tougher than metal fences. An electrifier in range powers it and its rods light up. Zombies can still bring it down.
Rods welded to the floor. An electrifier in range powers them. Each shock wears it down.
Aim and throw. Deals damage and may knock down. Anyone stepping in later gets shocked. The zone lasts 4 s. Right-click: change mode.
Aim and throw. Knocks down and slows anyone caught in the burst, without damage. Anyone stepping in later may fall. The zone lasts 5 s. Right-click: change mode.
Aim and throw. Very high damage and burns, but the zone only lasts 2 s.
Open it for building materials and a little Electrical experience. It may hold a SolarOS schematics magazine.
Aim and throw. Switches on after a few seconds and lasts 30 s: a barrier that slows and may knock down, with little damage. Right-click: change mode.
Aim and throw. Switches on after a few seconds and lasts 20 s: a barrier that slows, burns and deals more damage. Right-click: change mode.
